evidence_boundary: Official public agency pages and notices only; no station-level payload, private location, person-level warning record or operational telemetry was retrieved.

sources.title: Nino Tandilashvili on the expansion of the hydrometeorological observation network of the National Environmental Agency
Working Meeting Held on Multi-Hazard Forecasting Platforms and Early Warning Protocols

role_claims.claim: NEA describes its functions as establishing and operating meteorological, hydrological, geological and environmental monitoring systems; collecting and disseminating monitoring data; producing forecasts and issuing warnings within its competence; and providing warning information to central and local authorities and mass media.

The Hydrology Department describes stationary surface-water observation-network oversight, hydrological forecasts, preparation and distribution of warnings about expected hydrological events to decision-makers, interested persons and legal entities, and mass media; it also lists GIS integration and hydrological data-quality work.

The Geology Department lists regular geological monitoring, landslide and debris/mudflow monitoring, hazard-zoning maps, GIS catalogues, instrumental monitoring at extremely sensitive sites, fresh-drinking-groundwater monitoring and annual hydrogeological bulletins.

A 14 July 2026 NEA notice reports 278 hydrometeorological stations already installed and a target of 298 stations/watchpoints by the end of 2026; it also describes online data transmission and an introduced ICT system for collection, processing, analysis and warning dissemination.
The same 14 July 2026 NEA notice reports modern monitoring systems on 28 landslide bodies, including 22 integrated into one server platform.

A 26 December 2025 NEA workshop discussed proposals for multi-hazard forecasting platforms and early-warning protocols; the notice describes discussion and project direction, not formal adoption or operational completion.

not_established: The 298 year-end figure is a target stated on 2026-07-14, not evidence that 298 stations were installed or operational by 2026-11-28.
No current station inventory, hazard/region coverage, active/inactive dates, uptime, telemetry completeness, calibration or maintenance record was retrieved.
The notice does not provide hazard-specific forecast verification, lead-time distributions, probability of detection, false-alarm ratios or calibration metrics.
No separate counts or denominators were found for warnings issued, sent, delivered, acknowledged, understood, feasible to act on or acted on.
No active-user, app-delivery, accessibility, language-coverage or offline-channel performance data were published in the inspected pages.
The 2025 workshop notice does not establish that a national multi-hazard protocol was formally adopted, funded, operationalized or independently evaluated.
The agency-reported station and landslide-platform counts were not independently audited by NOEMA.
required_follow_up_metrics: Versioned station inventory by hazard, region and responsible department, with active dates, uptime, data completeness, calibration, maintenance and source provenance.
Hazard-specific forecast verification by lead time, including probability of detection, false-alarm ratio, critical success index, calibration and uncertainty.
Warning-event metadata with authority, hazard, geographic scope, issue/validity times, revisions, channel and pre-agreed action playbook identifiers.
Separate aggregate denominators for sent, delivered, acknowledged, understood, feasible and verified protective action; endpoint counts must not be labelled as people.
Evidence of formal protocol approval, responsible agencies, version, effective date, budget and after-action corrective-action closure.
Privacy-reviewed accessibility and language coverage, including non-digital channels, without person-level app telemetry or exact household locations in the public repository.

fact: NEA's public functions page assigns the Agency monitoring, data dissemination, forecasting, warning and hazard-risk participation functions within its competence.
NEA's Hydrology and Geology department pages describe distinct hydrological-forecast/warning and geological-monitoring/zoning responsibilities.

The 14 July 2026 notice reports 278 hydrometeorological stations installed, a target of 298 by year-end, and modern monitoring systems on 28 landslide bodies with 22 integrated into one server platform.
The 26 December 2025 notice records a workshop where multi-hazard forecasting-platform and early-warning-protocol proposals were discussed.
inference: The official material establishes institutional and technical capability signals, but not the completeness, reliability or equitable reach of the end-to-end warning chain.
The 278 installed count, 298 target and 28/22 landslide-platform counts measure different infrastructure outputs and must not be combined into one coverage percentage.
The next decision-relevant step is to connect an approved warning event to its issuing authority, forecast/station provenance, dissemination stages and feasible protective-action evidence.
hypothesis: A versioned, metadata-only authority and capability crosswalk linked to each authorised warning event could make missing ownership, provenance and warning-chain stages easier to identify without duplicating official warning issuance.
untested_idea: Build a read-only warning-event evidence registry that stores official reference IDs, authority, hazard, coarse area, issue/validity timestamps, source version, playbook version and aggregate stage denominators; keep all personal delivery telemetry outside the public system.
